name: A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems). Preprint arXiv:2502.12110 (cs.CL / cs.HC), v1 submitted 17 Feb 2025, last revised 8 Oct 2025 (v11).

Reproduction repo https://github.com/WujiangXu/A-mem actively maintained (vLLM/Ollama eval pipeline added Mar 2026).
task_domain: QA over long-term agent memory: long-range conversational question answering for LLM agents (single-hop, multi-hop, temporal-reasoning, open-domain, and adversarial QA). Framed as a memory system that LLM agents use to leverage historical experiences across extended dialogues.
problem_setting: Single-agent, online/streaming memory for LLM agents in long-term text conversations. Memory is built incrementally: as new interactions (dialogue turns/sessions) arrive, the system writes structured memory notes, links them to historical notes, and evolves existing notes. At query time the agent retrieves relevant historical memory to answer questions. No gradient training of the agent or retriever (LLM-driven, in-context); supervision is the QA answer labels of the benchmarks used only for evaluation, not for training. Backbone LLMs are swapped (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B, Llama-3.2-1B/3B, plus DeepSeek-R1-32B and Claude-3 Haiku in appendix). The setting is interactive memory construction over a single conversational agent, contrasted with static-corpus RAG and with rigid/predefined memory systems (MemGPT, MemoryBank, Mem0-style graph DB).
what_is_retrieved: Structured memory notes (experiences) distilled from past interactions. Each note bundles the original interaction content plus LLM-generated keywords, tags, and a contextual description, a dense embedding, a timestamp, and a set of links to related notes. Retrieval returns the top-k most relevant such notes (and, in the system design, linked notes within the same Zettelkasten 'box' are co-accessed).
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic self-written memory. A-Mem maintains no static external corpus/KB/API store; the retrievable store is an agent-written memory of past conversational interactions that grows online as new memories are added, with dynamic linking and memory evolution. (The related-work section explicitly contrasts this with static-knowledge-base agentic RAG.)
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective. Both link generation and query-time retrieval select the top-k notes by cosine similarity (default k=10, tuned per category up to 50). There is no minimal-complete-set or variable-size precision-driven objective; the hyperparameter study shows performance rising then plateauing/declining with larger k (noise vs context tradeoff).
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (embedding-similarity top-k recall of past notes), Reuse: yes (retrieved notes injected into the prompt as historical context for answering), Revise: partial-but-on-MEMORY (no per-query adaptation of a retrieved solution; instead, on each WRITE the system evolves/rewrites existing related notes' context/keywords/tags via memory evolution), Retain: yes (every new interaction is written as a structured note and linked into the network)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as an agentic memory system inspired by the Zettelkasten note-taking method and positioned against agent memory systems (MemGPT, MemoryBank, ReadAgent, SCM, Mem0) and RAG; it does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner and does not use the term 'case-based reasoning'. It realizes Retrieve/Reuse/Retain-like mechanisms under a memory-organization framing.
retrieval_unit: case/note granularity: a structured memory note (problem-context unit) = {original interaction content, timestamp, LLM-generated keywords, LLM-generated tags, LLM-generated contextual description, dense embedding, links}. Following Zettelkasten atomicity, each note is a single self-contained unit of knowledge; it is closest to a structured note / experience item, not a token snippet, full trajectory, tool-API, or executable skill.
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced. The store is built incrementally as interactions arrive; notes are added, linked, and evolved continuously (no offline pre-induced static index, no external corpus). In the official library this is a persistent ChromaDB vector store.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index augmented with an emergent LLM-generated link graph. Notes are embedded for nearest-neighbor cosine retrieval (flat vector index, O(N) storage), and on top of that the system autonomously generates links between notes, forming an interconnected Zettelkasten-style knowledge network of overlapping 'boxes' (a note can belong to multiple boxes). So topology = flat vector index + dynamic memory link graph (no predefined schema/hierarchy, deliberately unlike Mem0's predefined graph-DB schema).
retriever_type: Dense (embedding-based) retriever using cosine similarity over note embeddings produced by an off-the-shelf sentence encoder (all-MiniLM-L6-v2). An LLM is additionally used to decide which retrieved candidate notes to link/evolve, but the candidate retrieval itself is dense similarity (no BM25, no learned/generative retriever).
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf). Retrieval uses a frozen pretrained text encoder (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) with cosine similarity; there is no contrastive fine-tuning, LM-feedback retriever training, downstream-task RL, or value-based learning of the retriever. The 'agentic' learning happens in note generation, linking, and evolution via LLM prompting, not in a trained retriever.
query_construction: Raw query text. At inference the current interaction/question text q is embedded with the same encoder and matched against all note embeddings (eq = fenc(q)); no query decomposition, intent extraction, or synthetic-query expansion. (At write time the 'query' is the new note's full embedding over concat(content, keywords, tags, context) used to find nearest neighbors for linking.)
query_granularity: task/interaction-level (one-shot per query). Retrieval is performed once per current interaction/question using its embedding; not per-CoT-step or per-token. (Internally a two-step pattern exists: a write-time neighbor query when adding a memory, and a read-time query when answering, but each is a single one-shot similarity search.)
when_to_retrieve: one-shot per interaction. For each query the system performs a single top-k similarity retrieval to build the answering prompt; for each new memory it performs a single top-k neighbor retrieval to drive linking/evolution. No iterative, uncertainty-triggered, or learned-router re-retrieval within a single query.
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule. Retrieval is triggered unconditionally: once per incoming question (read path) and once per newly added memory note (write/link path). There is no token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated mid-step trigger; the 'agentic' decision is about linking/evolution, not about when to retrieve.
reranking: None. After dense top-k retrieval the notes are used directly (the LLM linking step is a connection/evolution decision, not a relevance reranker). No cross-encoder, RRF, hierarchy-aware, or instruction-tuned reranking stage is reported.
retrieved_context_refinement: Largely none at read time: top-k retrieved notes (and their linked notes in the same box) are injected into the prompt as historical context without compression/decomposition/distractor-filtering. The semantic enrichment (keywords/tags/context generation) and structural refinement (linking, evolution) happen at WRITE time, not as post-retrieval refinement of fetched items. The k-hyperparameter study notes large k introduces noise, motivating moderate k rather than an explicit refinement stage.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (A-Mem is a conversational memory system, not a tool/skill-retrieval method; there is no tool/API index).
index_content_separation: Partial. Each note stores lightweight semantic descriptors (keywords, tags, one-line contextual description) alongside the heavier original interaction content, and embeddings fuse both. However there is no explicit progressive-disclosure mechanism that retrieves a light index first and then loads heavy content on demand; whole notes are retrieved and injected.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool registry or integration protocol such as MCP/RapidAPI/RESTful/function-calling). The store is an internally managed growing note network; the official library persists it in ChromaDB and exposes CRUD (add/read/update/delete) over notes.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling; not a tool-retrieval method). The system does model inter-MEMORY relations via generated links, but not tool dependencies.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation. Retrieved top-k relevant memory notes (with their structured attributes and linked notes) are concatenated into the LLM's context to ground the answer to the current question. No fine-tuning, no latent-token injection; everything is in-context.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-answer (one-shot at query time). This is a QA/memory pipeline rather than a multi-step planner: for each question, retrieve top-k notes once, then generate the answer conditioned on them. The 'agentic' loop (note construction -> link generation -> memory evolution) runs on the WRITE/storage side as memories are ingested, not as an interleaved plan-time search. No MCTS/tree search, no per-step interleaved retrieval during answering.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer (per-question). Retrieval and memory injection occur once before generating the answer to a question and remain fixed for that answer. Not per-CoT-step, per-token, or per-tool-call.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted, applied to the MEMORY rather than to a single retrieved case: (1) note construction uses an LLM (template Ps1) to generate keywords/tags/context for each new interaction; (2) link generation uses an LLM (Ps2) to decide connections among the top-k nearest notes; (3) memory evolution uses an LLM (Ps3) to rewrite the context/keywords/tags of existing neighbor notes when a new note arrives, replacing the old note. There is no execution-feedback revision of a retrieved answer and no RL reuse-finetuning; reuse at answer time is verbatim-context injection.
retrieved_item_representation: Structured note (free text + metadata): injected items are human-readable notes carrying original content plus LLM-generated keywords, tags, and a contextual description, optionally with linked notes. Not raw trajectories, executable programs, or latent/soft tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Enriched/distilled note (single self-contained knowledge unit). It sits above a raw logged turn (because keywords/tags/contextual description abstract and re-describe the interaction) but below a generalized reusable workflow or procedural skill; it is an atomic, contextually-enriched experience note whose abstraction evolves over time via memory evolution.
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) Moderate top-k retrieval to balance context richness against retrieved noise (hyperparameter study shows gains plateau/decline at large k due to noise). (2) LLM-driven memory evolution that continuously refines/consolidates the contextual descriptions of existing notes, sharpening clusters (t-SNE shows more coherent clustering than base memory) and reducing dispersion. (3) Adversarial QA category in evaluation tests the ability to reject unanswerable queries. There is no retriever-aware contrastive training or explicit relevance-evaluator/self-reflection-filter on retrieved items.
memory_type: graph-structured episodic memory: a growing network of episodic interaction notes interconnected by LLM-generated semantic links (Zettelkasten knowledge network), stored as enriched structured text plus embeddings. Not a skill-library, procedural-policy, or latent memory.
write_back: Yes. Every new interaction is written back as a structured memory note (content + LLM-generated keywords/tags/context + embedding + links); the system additionally writes back UPDATES to existing neighbor notes during memory evolution. Closed loop: construct note -> retrieve neighbors -> generate links -> evolve neighbors -> store.
online_growth: Yes. The memory store grows continuously during deployment as interactions arrive (new notes added, links formed, neighbor notes evolved). Not frozen after an offline induction phase; the official library persists growth in ChromaDB.
write_back_trigger: always-on per-interaction (unconditional). A note is written for every incoming interaction regardless of success/failure (no success/failure gating, since this is QA-conversation memory rather than trajectory outcome memory); the same add event also triggers link generation and evolution of related historical notes. Not on-success-only, not reflective-after-critique, not human-validated.
failure_experience_usage: N/A / not distinguished. A-Mem stores conversational interactions as memory regardless of any task success/failure signal; it does not separate or contrastively use failed vs successful trajectories (no notion of negative/corrective experiences). Memory quality is improved via evolution/linking, not via failure labeling.
memory_evolution_update: link-and-evolve (refine-overwrite of existing entries). This is the work's defining mechanism: when a new note is added, the LLM may update the contextual descriptions, keywords, and tags of retrieved neighbor notes, and the evolved note replaces the original in the store (Eq. 7). Combined with dynamic link generation, the network self-organizes and continuously refines its understanding. Not purely append-only; supports delta-update/refine-overwrite of historical memories plus link formation. (CRUD update/delete also supported in the library.)
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Note selection (for linking and for answering) is fixed cosine-similarity top-k over frozen all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, not an RL- or value-optimized learned retrieval policy. The agentic behavior is LLM-prompted note enrichment/linking/evolution, not a trained retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory: one agent constructs and evolves its own A-Mem note network over its conversation history. No sharing of memory across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks is claimed.
benchmarks: LoCoMo (long-term conversational QA; ~9K tokens/dialogue, up to 35 sessions; 7,512 QA pairs across five categories: Multi-Hop, Temporal, Open-Domain, Single-Hop, Adversarial) as primary; DialSim (QA from long-term multi-party TV-show dialogues - Friends, The Big Bang Theory, The Office; ~1,300 sessions over five years, ~350K tokens) as secondary. Backbones: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B, Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3.2-3B (six foundation models in main tables), plus DeepSeek-R1-32B, Claude-3 Haiku, Claude-3.5 Haiku in the appendix. Scaling tested up to 1,000,000 memory entries.
benchmark_family: memory / long-context conversational QA (LoCoMo, DialSim). Within the survey's normalization this is the memory benchmark family (LoCoMo-style long-term conversation memory), with QA / multi-hop sub-types. No web, embodied, tool, code, or decision-RL benchmarks.
baselines: LoCoMo (full-context backbone LLM with no memory mechanism / full preceding conversation in prompt), ReadAgent (episode pagination + memory gisting + interactive look-up), MemoryBank (dynamic memory with Ebbinghaus-forgetting-curve updating and user-portrait building), and MemGPT (OS-inspired tiered virtual-context memory: main context = RAM, external context = disk). On DialSim only LoCoMo and MemGPT are compared. Mem0 (graph-DB memory) is discussed in the introduction/related work as motivation but is not a main results baseline.
key_metrics: Primary: F1 score (answer accuracy, harmonic mean of precision/recall) and BLEU-1 (unigram overlap). Efficiency: average answering token length per question; plus memory usage (MB) and retrieval time (microseconds) in the scaling study; processing time per memory op; per-op API cost. Appendix adds ROUGE-L, ROUGE-2, METEOR, and SBERT Similarity. A per-model average Ranking is also reported.
headline_result: On LoCoMo, A-Mem achieves the best average ranking across all six foundation models and roughly doubles (>=2x) baseline performance on complex Multi-Hop reasoning for GPT models, while using only ~1,200-2,500 answering tokens vs ~16,900 for full-context baselines (85-93% token reduction). Example (GPT-4o-mini): Temporal F1 45.85 vs MemGPT 25.52 / LoCoMo 18.41; overall best average ranking 1.2. On DialSim, A-Mem F1 = 3.45, a 35% improvement over LoCoMo (2.55) and 192% over MemGPT (1.18), and best across all six metrics (ROUGE-L 3.54, ROUGE-2 3.60, METEOR 2.05, SBERT 19.51).
ablations: (1) Module ablation (GPT-4o-mini, LoCoMo, Table 3): removing both Link Generation (LG) and Memory Evolution (ME) collapses performance (Multi-Hop F1 9.65, Single-Hop 13.28, Adversarial 15.32); adding LG only (w/o ME) recovers most (Multi-Hop 21.35, Single-Hop 39.17, Adversarial 44.16); full A-Mem is best (Multi-Hop 27.02, Temporal 45.85, Single-Hop 44.65, Adversarial 50.03), showing LG is the critical foundation and ME provides essential refinement. (2) Retrieval-k hyperparameter sweep (k = 10/20/30/40/50, Figure 3): performance rises then plateaus/slightly decreases at large k, most evident on Multi-Hop and Open-Domain (context-richness vs noise tradeoff). (3) Scaling study (Table 4): linear O(N) memory usage identical to baselines; A-Mem retrieval time grows only 0.31->3.70 microseconds from 1K to 1M entries (slightly slower than MemoryBank but far faster than ReadAgent's 43.6->120,069 microseconds). (4) Memory analysis: t-SNE shows A-Mem embeddings form more coherent clusters than base memory (without LG+ME).
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end QA metrics (F1, BLEU-1, ROUGE, METEOR, SBERT) plus efficiency metrics (token length, memory usage, retrieval time) are reported. No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k, nDCG, retrieval completeness) are separated from the downstream QA outcome; the closest decoupled signal is the retrieval-k hyperparameter sweep and the structural t-SNE memory analysis.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome-level (answer F1/BLEU/ROUGE/METEOR/SBERT). Some structural/process-adjacent analysis is provided qualitatively: the t-SNE memory-organization visualization (clustering coherence from LG+ME) and the per-category breakdown (e.g., multi-hop reasoning), plus efficiency proxies (tokens, retrieval latency). No step-wise retrieval accuracy or reasoning-faithfulness metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Strongly emphasized. A-Mem uses ~1,200 tokens per memory operation (answering ~1,126-2,520 tokens depending on model) vs ~16,900 for full-context LoCoMo/MemGPT, an 85-93% token reduction via selective top-k retrieval; each memory op costs <$0.0003 on commercial APIs. Processing ~5.4 s with GPT-4o-mini, ~1.1 s with local Llama-3.2-1B on one GPU. Scaling (Table 4): O(N) memory, retrieval time 0.31->3.70 microseconds across 1K->1M entries (orders of magnitude faster than ReadAgent). So large accuracy gains come with much lower inference cost than full-context baselines, despite multiple LLM calls during memory construction.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-k, default k=10 for query-time retrieval (tuned per LoCoMo category, swept over 10/20/30/40/50 in analysis), with top-k nearest-neighbor selection also used at link-generation time. Budget is effectively capped by the small retrieved-note set, yielding ~1,126-2,520 answering tokens. Not adaptive/precision-driven k and not reranked-then-truncated; k is a manually set hyperparameter (default 10, library default also k=10, recommended 3-10).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (no new benchmark constructed; uses existing LoCoMo - 7,512 QA pairs over five categories, ~9K-token dialogues up to 35 sessions - and DialSim - ~1,300 sessions, ~350K tokens, from three TV shows).
builds_on: Agent memory line: MemGPT (OS-style tiered context, Packer et al.), MemoryBank (Ebbinghaus-forgetting memory, Zhong et al.), ReadAgent (gist memory + interactive look-up), SCM (Self-Controlled Memory); structured/graph memory Mem0 (motivation/contrast). Conceptually inspired by the Zettelkasten note-taking method (Luhmann). Uses RAG foundations (Lewis et al.; standard dense-retrieval indexing) and the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence encoder for embeddings; evaluated on LoCoMo (Maharana et al.) and DialSim benchmarks; deployed via Ollama/LiteLLM and (in the library) ChromaDB.
contrasts_with: Memory systems with predefined/fixed structures and workflows that the agent must specify in advance: MemGPT (OS-style tiered context), MemoryBank, ReadAgent, SCM, and especially Mem0-style graph-database memory (predefined schemas/relationships limit adaptability). Also contrasts with agentic RAG (which is agentic only in the retrieval phase over a STATIC knowledge base) - A-Mem instead places agency in autonomous memory storage, linking, and evolution.
lineage: Group F (decision/memory line) - self-organizing agentic memory. Within the LLM-agent memory lineage (MemGPT -> MemoryBank/ReadAgent/SCM -> Mem0 graph memory -> A-Mem), A-Mem's distinctive contributions are (a) Zettelkasten-inspired note construction with LLM-generated keywords/tags/contextual descriptions, (b) autonomous LLM-driven link generation forming an interconnected, schema-free knowledge network, and (c) memory evolution that rewrites/refines existing historical notes when new memories arrive (self-organizing memory). It is a 2025 episodic-memory method emphasizing dynamic self-organization over fixed-structure storage and over static-corpus agentic RAG.
